findings.reason: the census's headline done-when is "every sourceless live name in exactly one of the five populations", so a name the ordered test leaves unplaced fails the node outright; the section must either state that `exhausted` in population 5 is descriptive rather than a filter or add the population that catches a non-exhausted name whose sources moved in-chain, and either edit changes what the classifier is told to compute.
findings.text: §35 asserts its five ordered populations are exhaustive ("they are tested in this order, and a name takes the first that applies, so every sourceless live name falls in exactly one"), but population 5 is gated on `exhausted and non-derived` and population 4 requires "at least one holder is not in the name's own REFINED_FROM, supersede or fold chain", so a live, non-derived, non-exhausted name whose every recorded source is held by an in-chain live name matches none of the five — and the section's own opening admits such names exist, counting 8 accepted and 14 at "other stages" among the 264 sourceless names
